title: A Frontend user whose commercial transporter is not one of the two on the list has no way to record it; Design release 1 lets them add one, giving its authorisation number, name, address and contact details

finding.frontend: The commercial branch is select-only. The page is a radio group and nothing else: two transporters, a Save and continue button, a Save and return to hub button and a Cancel link (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.njk:11-23). There is no add link, no add button and no add route — nothing in src/server matches a transporter add path — and the validator rejects any answer that is not one of the listed ids (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.controller.js:22-28). The private branch is not an escape either: it collects a name, an address and contact details but no transporter authorisation number, so it cannot stand in for a commercial transporter. A user whose commercial transporter is not one of the two is left with no way to record it. They are not stopped — they can go back to the type question and declare the same firm as a private transporter, typing its name and address by hand — but the notification then carries the wrong transporter type and no approval number at all.
finding.prototype: The transporter list carries an "Add a transporter" button under it (app/views/transporter.html:162-163). It leads to the type chooser, and choosing Commercial leads to a form headed "Add commercial transporter" under the caption "Add a new transporter". The form opens with a notification banner headed "Help with transporter authorisation" repeating the DAERA and APHA rules, then asks for: Transporter authorisation number; Name or organisation name; Address line 1; Address line 2 (optional); Town or city; County (optional); Postcode or Zip code; Country, which is fixed to Northern Ireland and cannot be changed; then, under a sub-heading "Enter contact details", Email address and Phone number hinted "For international numbers include the country code". The type chooser states the same restriction in words: Commercial is hinted "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland." The added transporter joins the list and can then be selected.
finding.difference: Add a page that lets a user enter a commercial transporter that is not on the list, reached from the transporter list rather than from the type question. It asks for a transporter authorisation number first, then name, the six address fields, a country locked to Northern Ireland, and an email address and phone number. The Northern Ireland restriction is a rule Design release 1 states twice and it has to be carried into the page and into the type chooser's hint. The frontend already stores a chosen commercial transporter as a name, an address and an approval number (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/transporters-select/transporters-select.controller.js:75-81), so a hand-entered one fits the answer shape that already exists and no contract outside the frontend has to change. This depends on the transporter list gaining an add route, which is the flow change raised beside it.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding any link, button or route in the frontend that lets a user enter a commercial transporter that is not in src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js.
finding.verification: Read both captured DOMs and both screenshots. Ran the falsifier by searching the whole of src/server for an add-transporter link, button or route: nothing matches, and the only transporter routes are the three declared at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/page.js. Read the validator at the cited lines — transporters-select.controller.js:22-28 is a oneOf over commercialTransporters.parties().map(o => o.id), so an id outside the fixture is rejected — and the answer shape at :75-81, which stores name, address and approvalNumber, confirming the finding's claim that a hand-entered transporter fits what is already saved. Checked the whole Design release 1 add-commercial form field by field against capture/html/prototype/dr1-transporter-add-commercial.html: the banner headed "Help with transporter authorisation", then transporterCommercialAuthorisationNumber, name, the six address fields, a Country control that is a disabled select showing Northern Ireland behind a hidden input of the same value, then the "Enter contact details" heading, email and a phone hinted for country codes — every item in the prototype slot is there and in that order. Also checked the brief's warning about Design release 1 contradicting itself over Northern Ireland: the rule appears exactly twice, on the add form's locked country and as the Commercial radio's hint in app/data/transporter-types.js:9, and both sit on the add route, so it constrains a transporter being added by hand rather than the pre-approved list — which is why the four non-Northern-Irish commercial rows on /transporter do not falsify it. Confirmed the frontend's own list carries a Swiss and a Belgian transporter, so the geography of either list is fixture data and not a finding.
finding.correction: The finding stands and is the right shape — one add-page finding with the missing content enumerated rather than one finding per field. Two things were wrong and have been fixed. First, the title said the user cannot go any further and the frontend slot said they are stopped. Following the journey rather than the page shows that is too strong: the commercial select page rejects anything outside its two ids, but its back link returns to the type question (transporters-select.controller.js:48), and the obligation model simply purges the commercial answer when the type flips to Private (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/transport.js:33-48), so the user can complete the notification by declaring the firm as a private transporter. What they cannot do is record it correctly, and both slots now say that. Second, the named control was "Add a transporter", which appears on neither of the two screens the finding attaches to — it is on dr1-transporter, which this finding does not name — so the crop could never have resolved and both cards would have fallen back to the whole page with a confusing reason printed. Since this is an add-page finding whose point is the whole missing form, the controls array is now empty, which is a stated choice the anchors report will list.

relatedTo.why: The add route this page needs is created by that flow change.
